evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost, and requires less time to build and launch.
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program for the reef

criteria.reasoning: All required introduction elements are present: mission, rationale, single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers. It is detailed, Australia-focused and well referenced, though some sources are non-scholarly.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning (UTC), and the mean pass lasts 580.8 s
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission.
The following STK 11 files are submitted with this report in ZYZZsat_STK.zip.

criteria.reasoning: Comprehensive mission design: launch choice, SSO elements, coverage, ground station, data budget, duration and EOL are supported by STK evidence and hand checks. Orbital and decay calculations are sound. Missing link budget and assumed ground-segment fit-out prevent full marks.

evidence.quote: ZYZZsat meets the mission needs set out in the introduction with one 50 kg satellite.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions follow directly from design evidence, summarise key performance values, and identify concrete limitations and next steps. Detailed and appropriate.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), a single Earth observation microsatellite for monitoring coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef.
Appendix A: STK files and settings

criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering-report structure, concise executive summary, readable prose, labelled figures/tables and consistent citation style. In-text citations match the bibliography. Minor presentation/reference-quality issues only.

technical_issues.issue: No full X-band link budget is presented; downlink feasibility is supported only by a simplified data-capacity calculation.
The design assumes S-band and X-band equipment can be added to the Mount Pleasant 12 m antenna, but this is not established.
Usable contact time is approximated as a fixed 60% of pass duration; actual elevation-dependent link capacity and pass scheduling are not modelled.
Vega C was unflown at the report date, and rideshare injection dispersion may not deliver exactly 600 km and 97.79° without propulsion.
The 'any reef within five days' claim uses equatorial track spacing and roll access; it is not a rigorous latitude/daylight/cloud coverage analysis.

overall: Strong, coherent mission design with accurate orbital, coverage, data-budget and decay calculations. All required elements are addressed and supported by STK screenshots/files. Main gaps are the absent X-band link budget and assumed ground-station fit-out; launch and revisit uncertainties are minor. Report structure and referencing are high quality.
